#load the libraries used in the project
library(readr)

#Question 1: We have already created the data folder

#Question 2

```{r}
# Load the main planet dataset
planets <- read_csv("data/Planet_list.csv")

# Verify dataset dimensions and data types of numerical variables
verification_table <- tibble(
  Check = c(
    "Number of rows is 866",
    "Number of columns is 8",
    "relative mass (earth) is numeric",
    "relative radius is numeric",
    "DENSITY (EARTH) is numeric"
  ),
  Passed = c(
    nrow(planets) == 866,
    ncol(planets) == 8,
    is.numeric(planets$`relative mass (earth)`),
    is.numeric(planets$`relative radius`),
    is.numeric(planets$`DENSITY (EARTH)`)
  )
)

# Display the verification results
verification_table
```
#Question 3

```{r}
# Scatter plot showing the relationship between planet density and relative radius
planets %>%
  filter(!is.na(`relative radius`), !is.na(`DENSITY (EARTH)`)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = `relative radius`, y = `DENSITY (EARTH)`)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6, color = "steelblue") +
  labs(
    title = "Planet Density vs. Relative Radius",
    x = "Relative Radius (Earth = 1)",
    y = "Density (Earth = 1)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

#Question 4

```{r}
# Compute summary statistics of planet relative mass
planet_mass_summary <- planets %>%
  summarise(
    Mean = mean(`relative mass (earth)`, na.rm = TRUE),
    Median = median(`relative mass (earth)`, na.rm = TRUE),
    `Standard Deviation` = sd(`relative mass (earth)`, na.rm = TRUE),
    `Interquartile Range` = IQR(`relative mass (earth)`, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = everything(),
    names_to = "Statistic",
    values_to = "Value"
  )

# Display the summary statistics table
planet_mass_summary
```
## Question 5

```{r}
# Compute the percentage of planets with a radius greater than Earth's radius
larger_planets_percentage <- planets %>%
  summarise(
    `Percentage larger than Earth (%)` = mean(`relative radius` > 1, na.rm = TRUE) * 100
  )

# Display the resulting percentage in a table
larger_planets_percentage
```
#Question 6

```{r}
# Identify the most extreme planets for each numerical variable
extreme_planets <- bind_rows(
  # Lowest and highest mass
  planets %>% 
    slice_min(`relative mass (earth)`, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>% 
    mutate(Characteristic = "Lowest mass"),
  planets %>% 
    slice_max(`relative mass (earth)`, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>% 
    mutate(Characteristic = "Highest mass"),
  
  # Smallest and largest radius
  planets %>% 
    slice_min(`relative radius`, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>% 
    mutate(Characteristic = "Smallest radius"),
  planets %>% 
    slice_max(`relative radius`, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>% 
    mutate(Characteristic = "Largest radius"),
  
  # Least dense and densest planets
  planets %>% 
    slice_min(`DENSITY (EARTH)`, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>% 
    mutate(Characteristic = "Least dense"),
  planets %>% 
    slice_max(`DENSITY (EARTH)`, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>% 
    mutate(Characteristic = "Densest")
) %>%
  select(
    Characteristic,
    Planet = P_NAME,
    `Relative Mass` = `relative mass (earth)`,
    `Relative Radius` = `relative radius`,
    `Density` = `DENSITY (EARTH)`
  )

# Display the extreme planets summary table
extreme_planets
```
## Question 7

```{r}
# Step 1: Count the number of planets orbiting each star
planets_per_star <- planets %>%
  count(Star_idx, name = "planet_count")

# Step 2: Plot the distribution of planet counts per star
ggplot(planets_per_star, aes(x = factor(planet_count))) +
  geom_bar(fill = "steelblue") +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of the Number of Planets per Star",
    x = "Number of Planets per Star",
    y = "Number of Stars"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
## 2 Star data

## Question 8

```{r}
# Load the star dataset
stars <- read_csv("data/DATA-STARS.csv")

# Quick check on the number of stars loaded (expected: 561 rows)
nrow(stars)
```
## Question 9

```{r}
# Split the stellar type into three separate columns: temp_class, magnitude, and luminosity_class
stars <- stars %>%
  separate_wider_delim(
    cols = `Type Of Star`,
    delim = "|",
    names = c("temp_class", "magnitude", "luminosity_class")
  )

# Preview the newly separated columns
stars %>%
  select(STAR, temp_class, magnitude, luminosity_class) %>%
  head()
```
## Question 10

```{r}
# Compute the average mass of stars per temperature class
avg_star_mass_per_class <- stars %>%
  group_by(temp_class) %>%
  summarise(
    `Average Mass (Solar Masses)` = mean(`relative mass`, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

# Display the summary table
avg_star_mass_per_class
```
## 3 Combined analysis

## Question 11

```{r}
# Identify all unique stars that host at least one planet
stars_with_planets <- planets %>%
  distinct(Star_idx)

# Compute the number of stars without any planets
stars_without_planets <- stars %>%
  filter(!Star_idx %in% stars_with_planets$Star_idx) %>%
  summarise(
    `Number of Stars Without Planets` = n()
  )

# Display the result
stars_without_planets
```
## Question 12

```{r}
# Step 1: Compute average planet radius for each star
avg_planet_radii <- planets %>%
  group_by(Star_idx) %>%
  summarise(
    avg_planet_radius = mean(`relative radius`, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

# Step 2: Combine with the star dataset using inner_join
star_planet_radius <- inner_join(avg_planet_radii, stars, by = "Star_idx")

# Step 3: Filter out missing values to eliminate warnings, then plot
star_planet_radius %>%
  filter(!is.na(`Star Radius`), !is.na(avg_planet_radius)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = `Star Radius`, y = avg_planet_radius)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6, color = "steelblue") +
  labs(
    title = "Average Planet Radius vs. Star Radius",
    x = "Star Radius (Solar Radii)",
    y = "Average Planet Radius (Earth Radii)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
## 4 Planet characteristics

## Question 13

```{r}
# Extract terrain types into a dedicated two-column data frame
planet_terrains <- planets %>%
  select(Planet_number, Terrain) %>%
  separate_longer_delim(Terrain, delim = "|")

# Extract climate types into a dedicated two-column data frame
planet_climates <- planets %>%
  select(Planet_number, Type_climate) %>%
  separate_longer_delim(Type_climate, delim = "|")

# Preview the first few rows of each newly created data frame
head(planet_terrains)
head(planet_climates)
```
## Question 14

```{r}
# Step 1: Count the number of distinct terrain types per planet
terrains_per_planet <- planet_terrains %>%
  filter(!is.na(Terrain)) %>%
  distinct(Planet_number, Terrain) %>%
  count(Planet_number, name = "nb_terrains")

# Step 2: Plot the distribution of terrain type counts per planet
ggplot(terrains_per_planet, aes(x = factor(nb_terrains))) +
  geom_bar(fill = "forestgreen") +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of the Number of Different Terrain Types per Planet",
    x = "Number of Different Terrain Types",
    y = "Number of Planets"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
## Question 15

```{r}
# Prepare data: extract planet mass and expand the climate multivalued variable
planet_mass_by_climate <- planets %>%
  select(Planet_number, `relative mass (earth)`, Type_climate) %>%
  separate_longer_delim(Type_climate, delim = "|") %>%
  filter(!is.na(Type_climate), !is.na(`relative mass (earth)`))

# Represent graphically the distribution of planet mass conditioned by climate
ggplot(planet_mass_by_climate, aes(x = Type_climate, y = `relative mass (earth)`)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "lightblue", outlier.size = 1.2) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of Planet Mass Conditioned by Climate",
    x = "Climate Type",
    y = "Relative Mass (Earth = 1, Log10 Scale)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```
## Question 16

```{r}
# Compute the total number of distinct climates seen on planets orbiting each star
climates_per_star <- planets %>%
  select(Star_idx, Type_climate) %>%
  separate_longer_delim(Type_climate, delim = "|") %>%
  filter(!is.na(Type_climate)) %>%
  group_by(Star_idx) %>%
  summarise(
    `Number of Distinct Climates` = n_distinct(Type_climate)
  )

# Display the summary table
climates_per_star
```
